# Wheat flour

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the wheat flour came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-wheat-flour" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-wheat-flour-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of wheat flour, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

quartile) and 10 µg/kg (upper quartile).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, wheat flour, flour or meal had the lowest cadmium subgroup median in PAHO (22.7 µg/kg) and the highest in EMRO (23.8 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Targeted wheat flour, as sold samples in EURO had cadmium lower at 12 µg/kg, against 20 µg/kg for EURO in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

In one study, lead across 15 groups of wheat flour ranged from 29 µg/kg (Autumn 2016) to 87 µg/kg (Autumn 2017); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/noori2022-khuzestan-wheat-flour-lead-cadmium|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Noori SMA, Zadehdabagh R, Najafi N, Tishezan L, Zerehpoush M, Mousavi Jazayeri SMH, Hashemi M, Tavakoly Sany SB · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/noori2022-khuzestan-wheat-flour-lead-cadmium">Measurement of the Toxic Trace Elements in Commercial Wheat Flours: Potential Health Risk via Dietary Intake</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Chemical Health Risks 12(4), 713-724</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/noori2022-khuzestan-wheat-flour-lead-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, cadmium across 20 groups of wheat flour ranged from 6.56 µg/kg (Heilongjiang province/city, national sampling 2023-2024) to 22.7 µg/kg (Henan province/city, national sampling 2023-2024); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/zhang2025-china-grain-products-cadmium-risk|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Zhang Q, Dou W, Wang Z, Xu X, Jiang T · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/zhang2025-china-grain-products-cadmium-risk">Safety Risk Assessment and Classification of Cadmium in Grain Processing Products</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 2025, 14(11), 1882</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/zhang2025-china-grain-products-cadmium-risk">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<a id="procurement-and-process-control"></a>
## Buying and verifying wheat flour

<a id="hmi-ing-028"></a>
<a id="what-origin-traceability-processing-and-analytical-information-should-a-buyer-request"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-029"></a>
<a id="which-control-or-specification-choices-are-supported-and-which-are-policy-choices-requiring-separate-justification"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-030"></a>
<a id="what-supplier-process-or-test-result-changes-should-trigger-investigation-or-requalification"></a>

No maximum level for metals in wheat flour was verified from primary text for this page; buyers should confirm the limit that applies in the destination market.



<a id="finished-product-and-exposure-implications"></a>
## Exposure from wheat flour

<a id="hmi-ing-031"></a>
<a id="how-do-inclusion-rate-processing-yield-preparation-and-other-ingredients-affect-a-finished-product-estimate"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-032"></a>
<a id="how-do-consumption-patterns-and-intended-populations-affect-dietary-exposure-interpretation"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-033"></a>
<a id="what-conclusions-require-finished-product-measurements-or-a-separate-exposure-assessment"></a>

No source in the library converted wheat flour concentrations into a verified estimate of intake for a defined population. Concentrations describe the food, not individual risk.



<a id="requirements-evidence-assessment-and-updates"></a>
## Evidence review and remaining gaps

<a id="hmi-ing-034"></a>
<a id="which-primary-regulatory-instruments-apply-to-this-exact-ingredient-form-species-market-and-date"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-035"></a>
<a id="what-searches-eligibility-decisions-source-families-and-appraisal-underpin-the-answers-and-certainty-judgments"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-036"></a>
<a id="what-remains-unresolved-when-was-each-answer-reviewed-and-what-changed-in-this-version"></a>

Every source record that names wheat flour was decided on its content: 29 occurrence extracted, 29 records in all. The occurrence table renders every extracted result; held values remain visible with their reason.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.

<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in wheat flour?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, B, Ba, Ca, K, <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-wheat-flour" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-wheat-flour" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in wheat flour?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in wheat flour?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, wheat flour, flour or meal had the lowest cadmium subgroup median in PAHO (22.7 µg/kg) and the highest in EMRO (23.8 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-wheat-flour-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-wheat-flour-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in wheat flour is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in wheat flour is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 6 results from 3 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span
